"Regular evening rules for supply orders"
This section describes the standard that applies to Companion Animal Travel Desk handling of companion animal bookings, from first contact through arrival support.

Aurelia Skyways expects staff to give clear, calm guidance and to record each request in the booking file before any travel promise is made. The Companion Animal Travel Desk should check that the traveler understands crate care, cabin or hold limits, feeding instructions, and any airport handoff steps that may affect a smooth journey. When a case involves a rabbit, <<FACT F070>> Staff must keep the discussion practical and avoid adding promises that have not been confirmed by the carrier or the relevant station team.

For bird travel, the desk must confirm the health paperwork is present, readable, and current before the booking moves forward. <<FACT F083>> If a document is missing or unclear, staff should pause the release of travel approval and guide the traveler toward the next safe step. The same careful review applies when an animal has special feeding needs, mobility limits, or a planned transfer between skyports.

The desk should also watch for signs that the owner needs extra support with timing, check-in flow, or arrival pickup. When a traveler asks for help, staff may explain the process in plain language and note any agreed service point in the file. If a pet such as Archie is listed in the reservation, the record must match the approved details exactly so that ground teams can follow the same plan without confusion. Keep messages polite, brief, and consistent with the safety-first standard used across Aurelia Skyways.

When a case cannot be resolved at desk level, escalate it to the senior coordinator and keep the traveler informed in steady, respectful terms. For further guidance, contact the Companion Animal Travel Desk.
